lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Match each habit to a respectful action: confirm local name; credit a story; follow safety rules for plants.

FEEDBACK
Confirm local name by asking local sources; credit a story by naming storyteller and Nation; follow safety by not eating wild plants without an expert.

WATCH FOR
A poster of pictures with no sources or protocols shows decoration instead of respectful learning.

teach_steps.explain:
The First Nations unit review connects diversity of Nations, Acknowledgement of Country, connection to Country, seasonal calendars, story protocols, technology, bush food care and contributions today. The key habit is respect: ask, credit and use community-approved sources.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner base claims on sources, places and respectful community knowledge, rather than guessing from a single picture. Keep every claim linked to evidence.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the sources, map features or community examples that carry the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Compare your record with the feedback: did you use the same skill and show your evidence? If a detail is uncertain, identify what source you would need next. One deliberate, evidence-based revision is more useful than writing a longer answer.
